about.title: Morro Bay Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Morro Bay is a small coastal community, but defective products cause harm here just as they do anywhere else — a corroded bike part on the Embarcadero, a malfunctioning kitchen appliance, a piece of fishing or boating equipment that fails without warning. California product liability law is built around strict liability, which means an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product had a defect (in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings) and that the defect caused the injury. That distinction matters because it can simplify what would otherwise be a difficult burden of proof. If you were hurt by something that didn't work the way it was supposed to, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who evaluates these claims regularly and can explain, without cost or obligation, what your options may be under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Product Liability Claims Work Differently

items.title: Strict Liability Can Ease Your Burden
items.desc: California generally doesn't require proof the manufacturer was negligent — showing the product was defective and caused harm may be enough. This can make these claims more direct than typical negligence cases.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product, which may widen the pool of parties an attorney can pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any manuals intact is often critical to proving the defect existed — an attorney can advise you on how to safely preserve this evidence.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability framework generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused your injury, not on what the manufacturer knew or intended. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your situation and explain how this might apply.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the item exactly as it was at the time of the injury, along with any packaging, receipts, or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw anything away. This evidence can be important if a claim moves forward.

items.question: Is this relevant if my injury happened somewhere ordinary in Morro Bay, like my kitchen or garage?
items.answer: Yes — product defect claims aren't limited to industrial settings. Whether the incident happened at home, on a boat near the harbor, or along South Bay Boulevard, what matters is the product and the defect, not the location.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
